auditRule: Evidence lineage, not URL count, controls independence. Primary manuscripts/material objects and institutional histories are separated from retrospective synthesis. A Deep Anchor may be source-locked with a named boundary when the missing evidence is irrelevant to the locked claim but must not silently inherit precision it does not possess.

independentLineages: Science Museum Group British material history
anchors.primaryEvidence: 1837 U.S. Congressional telegraph report, 1844 line artifacts/messages and Vail operating/business archive
anchors.rivalFailureEvidence: Cooke–Wheatstone system, optical telegraph incumbent and U.S. patent/credit/business disputes
anchors.boundary: The U.S. lineage is much richer than the British primary lineage in this batch. Any fine-grained priority claim about Cooke versus Wheatstone requires dedicated British patent/correspondence evidence; current evidence is sufficient for parallel-system/network reconstruction only.

independentLineages: Science Museum Group electrical-instrument material history
anchors.primaryEvidence: physical/visual expedition records for 1857/1858/1865/1866 and cable-laying/recovery operations
anchors.rivalFailureEvidence: temporary 1858 cable, 1865 near-completion break, weak-signal versus stronger-drive operating choices
anchors.boundary: The exact causal partition of the 1858 failure among manufacturing defects, insulation damage and high-voltage operation remains disputed. HD2 locks only the stronger fact that first communication did not establish durable service and that electrical/mechanical/material design all entered the correction process.

independentLineages: Royal Society primary Joule manuscript/referee archive
anchors.primaryEvidence: Joule 1849 mechanical-equivalent manuscript plus contemporary referee record
anchors.rivalFailureEvidence: caloric theory, multiple independent conservation formulations, early sensitivity limits and later Joule–Thomson refinement
anchors.boundary: The batch does not bind primary Mayer/Helmholtz/Clausius manuscripts individually. It is sufficient for the distributed quantitative-conservation/temperature/measurement trajectory; exact priority or textual ontology claims require those primary works.

independentLineages: Science Museum Group Wheatstone material object
anchors.primaryEvidence: Faraday 1831 induction manuscript/apparatus and surviving 1866 Wheatstone dynamo
anchors.rivalFailureEvidence: permanent-magnet magneto route and near-simultaneous self-excitation claims
anchors.boundary: Siemens' 1866 self-excitation evidence in this batch is company-archive retrospective evidence rather than an original paper/patent. Do not use A04 for exact Siemens/Wheatstone/Varley priority ordering without a separate primary-source audit.

anchors.primaryEvidence: material cameras/process artifacts are mediated through museum catalogues; this batch has no direct scanned French disclosure decree or Talbot patent text
anchors.rivalFailureEvidence: Daguerre unique-positive route, Talbot negative-positive route, wet-collodion replacement and Pencil of Nature production friction
anchors.boundary: The process tradeoffs and succession are well supported, but quantitative causal claims about how much patents slowed British photography require economic/adoption evidence beyond this bundle.

independentLineages: Science Museum Group Bessemer material history
anchors.primaryEvidence: 1860 Bessemer steel sample and 1865 pilot converter, with Bessemer 1856 paper/work chronology in institutional catalogue
anchors.rivalFailureEvidence: early feedstock-quality failure, Mushet correction lineage, phosphorus limitation and open-hearth competition
anchors.boundary: The batch supports the general correction-rich feedstock/composition story. It does not justify a precise claim that one Mushet addition alone solved all early failures; phosphorus and other ore/composition variables remained distinct.

schemaAudit.finding: Telegraph networks, repeated submarine infrastructure failure, distributed thermodynamic theory, generator feedback, photographic process plurality and steel process correction are all representable in the existing trajectory schema. The new friction remains source-lineage precision and causal attribution, not missing ontology.
schemaAudit.decision: Keep the trajectory schema frozen. Record source/causal precision as evidence-boundary metadata rather than inventing a new historical schema mid-wave.
